Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Agribusiness | National NADKANSCO targets export market with cashew kernels, shell liquid and briquettes Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:06pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman is preparing to supply international markets with processed cashew products, including cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid and briquettes, as Ghana intensifies efforts to add value to its agricultural produce.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank), Sylvester Adinam Mensah, disclosed this during the commissioning of the factory by President John Dramani Mahama in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026.
He said the facility would also produce cashew-based products for the domestic market as part of efforts to expand the range of goods manufactured locally.
“Today, NADKANSCO is ready to export the following: cashew nuts of all grades, cashew nut shell liquid, briquettes, all for the foreign market,” he said.
“For the local market, NADKANSCO is ready to sell cashew cakes, briquettes and roasted kernels,” the CEO added.
Mr Mensah said the factory represented a major step towards retaining more economic value from Ghana's cashew production instead of exporting the nuts in their raw state for processing elsewhere.
He noted that Ghana produced more than 262,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts last year, but only 17,000 metric tonnes were processed locally.
According to him, the NADKANSCO facility has an installed capacity to process up to 33,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew annually, creating opportunities for increased production, employment and export earnings.
The Ghana EXIM Bank CEO said the bank had committed approximately $12 million to support the project, including funding for automated processing equipment, working capital and workforce training.
The factory has already created nearly 1,000 direct jobs and supports an additional 3,000 livelihoods across the cashew value chain.
Mr Mensah said the investment would help create jobs, strengthen local industries and support farmers by providing a ready market for their produce.
He urged the company's management to scale up operations and utilise the facility's full production capacity, assuring them of the bank's continued commitment to the project.
